prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project manages its releases through a defined LTS (Long Term Support) schedule, which is broken down into distinct phases. According to the official Node.js Release documentation, an LTS release goes through an "Active" phase and a "Maintenance" phase, each lasting for a specified duration.

Here are the official details regarding the duration of these phases:

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-plan | QUOTE: "Once a release moves into Active LTS, it remains in that phase for 12 months." | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase lasts for 12 months.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-plan | QUOTE: "After the 12 months of Active LTS, the release moves into Maintenance LTS, where it remains for a period of 18 months." | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase lasts for 18 months.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A separate official page outside of the core Node.js GitHub repository that documents the exact month durations of the Active and Maintenance phases (the primary and most cited official source for the lifecycle schedule is the `nodejs/Release` repository on GitHub).
